lines: The watchtower is derelict but standing. Stairs lead to an observation platform where a battered telescope still points toward the horizon.
A small inner room is sealed behind a door. Dust covers everything.
You press your eye to the scope. The optics are cracked but functional.
To the south: the distant glow of Meridian City on the horizon, a warm amber smear against the dark.
To the north: nothing but black for hundreds of kilometers. Except — there. A Lighthouse beam, flickering erratically. Lighthouse Mara.
The beam is sputtering. Dying. Between the flickers, you can see shapes moving in the darkness around its base.
Whatever is happening at Lighthouse Mara, it's getting worse.
A worn observation journal. The entries span decades, each one meticulously recording the position of the light's edge.
"Year 12: Floodlight perimeter stable at 400 meters. No incursions."
"Year 19: Perimeter pulled back to 200 meters. Lost Floodlight 3 and 7."
"Year 24: Perimeter at 50 meters. The watchtower is now in darkness. I can hear them outside."
The last entry: "The light went out."
The Old Keeper at Outpost Balor served on the perimeter for years. He'd want to read this.
